title: Henselianity descends through a quotient inside the maximal ideal
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring whose maximal-ideal pair is henselian in the idempotent-lifting sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Then the pair $(A/I,\mathfrak m/I)$ is henselian: for every finite $(A/I)$-algebra $B$, every idempotent of $B/(\mathfrak m/I)B$ lifts to a unique idempotent of $B$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 09XK (label lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2753) applied to the surjection $A\to A/I$, as in the proof of (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of Lemma 0DYD (label lemma-henselian-henselian-pair, line 2785); with the definition in its finite-algebra form (characterization (3) of Lemma 09XI) in place of the integral form (4)

proof.text: *A finite $A/I$-algebra is a finite $A$-algebra.* Let $\pi:A\to A/I$ be the quotient map and let $B$ be a finite $A/I$-algebra with structure map $\psi:A/I\to B$, so $B=\sum_{k=1}^n\psi(A/I)\,b_k$ for some $b_1,\dots,b_n\in B$. Regard $B$ as an $A$-algebra via $\psi\circ\pi$. Since $\pi$ is surjective, every element $\sum_k\psi(\bar a_k)b_k$ with $\bar a_k\in A/I$ equals $\sum_k(\psi\circ\pi)(a_k)b_k$ for any lifts $a_k\in A$ of $\bar a_k$; hence $b_1,\dots,b_n$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module and $B$ is a finite $A$-algebra.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 09XK (label lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2753) applied to the surjection $A\to A/I$, as in the proof of (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of Lemma 0DYD (label lemma-henselian-henselian-pair, line 2785); with the definition in its finite-algebra form (characterization (3) of Lemma 09XI) in place of the integral form (4)

proof.text: *The two ideals of $B$ agree.* Write $\mathfrak m/I=\pi(\mathfrak m)$, an ideal of $A/I$ because $\pi$ is surjective. The ideal $(\mathfrak m/I)B$ of $B$ is generated by $\psi(\pi(\mathfrak m))$, and the ideal $\mathfrak mB$ of the $A$-algebra $B$ is generated by the image $(\psi\circ\pi)(\mathfrak m)$ of $\mathfrak m$ under the structure map: the same set of generators. Hence $(\mathfrak m/I)B=\mathfrak mB$, and $B/(\mathfrak m/I)B$ and $B/\mathfrak mB$ are the same quotient ring of $B$, with the same quotient map $q:B\to B/\mathfrak mB$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 09XK (label lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2753) applied to the surjection $A\to A/I$, as in the proof of (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of Lemma 0DYD (label lemma-henselian-henselian-pair, line 2785); with the definition in its finite-algebra form (characterization (3) of Lemma 09XI) in place of the integral form (4)

proof.text: *Lifting.* The pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $B$ is a finite $A$-algebra by step 1, so every idempotent $\bar e$ of $B/\mathfrak mB$ is $q(e)$ for a unique idempotent $e\in B$. By step 2 this says: every idempotent of $B/(\mathfrak m/I)B$ lifts to a unique idempotent of $B$ (the set of idempotents of $B$ does not depend on the base ring). As $B$ was an arbitrary finite $A/I$-algebra, $(A/I,\mathfrak m/I)$ is a henselian pair in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

Statement unchanged and checked (case I=m: A/I a field, pair (k,0), trivially henselian). Proof in three elementary steps: a finite A/I-algebra is finite over A through the surjection; (m/I)B = mB as ideals of B; the definition for (A,m) then gives unique idempotent lifting modulo (m/I)B. No new node needed: no integrality or finite-transitivity node is used because the surjection makes finiteness immediate.
